Devon: FYI seeing a latency spike and throughput drop on prod-serving starting ~09:12 UTC, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 520ms, p99 ~1.8s. Throughput down ~30%.
Miguel: looking now, any service/route specifics?
Devon: mostly text-generation v2 routes hitting dedicated pool A, spike coincides with a canary rollout from last night (kernel-selector tweak).
Anya: adding metrics: KV cache miss rate increased 8% -> 42% around the same time, warm-pool fill rate shows stalls (provision step waiting ~600-1200ms extra per instance).
Rachel: @sre-bot can you dump recent kernel selection logs and batch size distribution for pool A?
sre-bot: actioned. attaching snippets: `kernel_selector: scored kernels: [fast_attn:0.34, generic:0.66]` and `batch_size_dist: {1: 54%, 2: 28%, >=4: 18%}`
Zach: kernel score flipping to generic at scale is suspicious — that increases per-token cost and often adds 200-400ms on cold joins. Did the canary change thresholds?
Miguel: I pulled the git diff from the canary rollout: we relaxed the noise_threshold in kernel heuristics to reduce churn, but the metric we used was microbench median latency; under variance it pushes selection toward generic kernel.
Devon: so combination: kernel selector prefers generic -> higher CPU usage -> slower provisioning -> warm pool stalls -> more cold joins -> KV cache rebuilds = cascading latency.
Anya: I profiled a cold join: attached flame snippet (short):
```
flamegraph: 09:14:23
gpu_copy -> 35%
kernel_launch -> 28%
kv_cache_load -> 22%
serialization -> 10%
others -> 5%
```
Miguel: kv_cache_load dominating cold joins. I also see repeated small OOM events on node-nn-12 before the spike, kubelet evicted large caches. Kernel fallback selection happened after the OOM backlog.
Rachel: any noisy neighbor evidence? node-nn-12 had another tenant with heavy memcpy bursts at 09:10 per node metrics. network rx/tx spikes correlated.
Zach: that aligns: memcpy bursts + kernel fallback = degraded perf. Can we confirm kernel microbench noise coincided with memcpy bursts?
Miguel: yes, microbench variance increased at 09:09:50 on nodes with high memcpy. The kernel selector uses a short rolling window (30s) so it flipped.
Devon: immediate mitigation suggestions?
Anya: 1) revert the heuristic change to noise_threshold to previous value (fast to ship) 2) increase warm-pool target by +15% for pool A temporarily 3) reduce scale-down cooldown to allow faster reprovisioning 4) pin KV cache eviction policy to be less aggressive (nudge kube osm config).
Rachel: I'll open a rollback PR for the heuristic and request an emergency rollout. Devon, can you bump the warm pool target and adjust cooldown?
Devon: on it. running `infractl pool update --name=pool-A --target=+15% --scale-cooldown=30s`
deploy-bot: rollout started for revert-pr#4123 (kernel-heuristic-revert) to pool A canary -> 2/3 hosts updated
Anya: while revert is rolling, we should also throttle the noisy tenant on node-nn-12. @Miguel can you coordinate with infra to cordon it?
Miguel: cordoning node-nn-12 now and draining heavy tenant pods. `kubectl cordon node-nn-12` -> `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node-nn-12`
Zach: after cordon, microbench variance dropped back to baseline within ~40s on other nodes. kernel selector started preferring fast_attn again.
Devon: warm pool fill latency reduced from +1.1s to +180ms after cordon and revert continued rollout. p95 down to 150ms, p99 ~420ms, throughput back to ~95% of baseline.
Rachel: nice. Any remaining root-cause follow-ups?
Miguel: postmortem items: 1) kernel selector sensitivity too aggressive to short window variance -> change to a longer smoothing window + require sustained regressions before switching; 2) make KV cache eviction resilient across node OOMs (persist across restarts where possible); 3) add preflight noisy-neighbor detector to avoid mixing noisy tenants with latency-sensitive pools; 4) add warm-pool overprovision soft buffer when KV cache miss-rate > 20%.
Anya: I'll draft the postmortem and link profiling artifacts and the flamegraph. Also adding a perf test that injects memcpy noise to validate selector stability.
Devon: immediate follow-ups done: revert merged and finished, pool target bumped, node cordoned and drained. Monitoring for 60m.
Rachel: marking this as incident-low-impact but P1-ish for runtime perf. Logging follow-ups to tracker: PERF-789, INFRA-344, KERNEL-512.
Miguel: I'll own the kernel selector changes (KERNEL-512), aim to land a safer heuristic by end of next week.
Devon: thanks everyone. I'll close the loop after 60m and post a short blameless summary. :thumbsup:
Rachel: great job. :clap:
sre-bot: incident timeline saved to #incidents with id INC-2026-042.
Devon: closing thread, last check at 10:05 UTC looked stable.
